title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory trial (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) measuring whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style verifier into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered contract enforced shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both arms) to isolate repair-mediated differences from generator sampling variance. We ran 200 paired tasks (50 per prespecified stratum: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) with declared generator gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). All archived scoring artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair_count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We reconcile this degenerate null to the preregistered design choices, present deterministic validator semantics that define the primary outcome, give execution accounting and diagnostics grounded in archived artifacts, and discuss construct/internal/external validity implications and reproducible follow-ups.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent-to-configuration translation using large language models (LLMs) promises operational productivity gains but raises acute safety concerns: an incorrect command may cause outages, violate security policy, or create routing instability. A common mitigation is a generate→validate→repair workflow in which a deterministic verifier (sandbox) flags semantic or policy violations and an automated repair or human gate corrects or blocks unsafe proposals. Prior work proposes verifier-in-the-loop architectures, but rigorous quantification of a verifier’s marginal benefit—separating repair-mediated corrections from generator sampling variance—remains limited.

We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 to answer a focused confirmatory question: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors compared to LLM-only generation when the initial generation is shared between arms (shared_initial_generation)? Shared_initial_generation intentionally isolates repair-mediated differences: any paired discordance must originate from repair activity. Our contributions are: (1) a sealed preregistered paired-trial design that enforces shared_initial_generation to attribute repair effects causally; (2) a completed, fully archived execution on 200 paired tasks balanced across four prespecified strata with deterministic per-episode validator traces; and (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation of a degenerate null outcome with specific, reproducible follow-ups.
sections.related_work: LLM applications to NetOps (intent-driven synthesis, constrained generation for virtualized network functions, prototype remediation loops) are active research topics (Nguyen Tu et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2025; NetSoft 2024; ICNP 2025). Generate→validate→repair and bounded self-correction patterns appear repeatedly as operational mitigations (Sang 2025; Okula 2026). Surveys and architecture papers emphasize that operational reliability is as much an architectural property (tool integration, audit traces, human gates) as it is a model capability (Bilal et al., 2026; Malik 2026). Separate lines develop failure-mode taxonomies and recommend layered runtime defenses and auditability (Maharaj 2026; Vadlamudi 2026). Our study differs by preregistering a single primary estimand in a paired design, enforcing shared_initial_generation to attribute any effect specifically to repair, and fully archiving deterministic per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to enable exact diagnostics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration, estimand, and design: The study was sealed before execution (preregistration_sha256: aa4055d52c118741524c4c42d07efa977372be338b9bd96069dc7abfc5b32ac4). Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline), where a task is 'validator-clean' if the deterministic validator reports zero violations on the final configuration. The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05); paired 95% percentile bootstrap CIs use 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Sample, strata, and inclusion rules: The confirmatory sample comprised 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks in a paired design (200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 episodes). Tasks were deterministically generated and balanced across four prespecified strata: IOS-like single-step (n = 50), IOS-like multi-step (n = 50), JunOS-like single-step (n = 50), JunOS-like multi-step (n = 50). These stratum counts were enforced by the deterministic task generator and recorded in the authoritative task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b). The manifest includes per-task difficulty labels and full task payloads; researchers should consult that artifact for per-task metadata.

Shared_initial_generation contract and adapter semantics: To attribute differences specifically to repair activity, the preregistered contract produced one initial model generation per task and reused that candidate for both baseline and guarded evaluations (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). Execution used a hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter implementing bounded generate→validate→repair with at most one repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The declared generator in the archived execution configuration is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider accounting confirms one model call per task (model_calls_used = 200; maximum_model_calls permitted = 400).

Deterministic validator (harm-oracle) semantics: The primary validator is a deterministic Batfish-style verifier implemented in the harness and recorded per episode. For clarity we enumerate the validator failure categories used to define the primary outcome (each appears in per-episode validator_trace fields): (1) reachability violations — required intent-prescribed paths absent after applying the candidate; (2) ACL/policy violations — contradictions with intent-enforced permit/deny constraints; (3) routing anomalies — loops, next-hop mismatches, or blackholes inconsistent with intent; (4) interface-state and workflow invariant violations — make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore, one-of-N uplink constraints; (5) dangerous-command flags — matches to regex-based forbidden-command detectors. Per-episode traces record validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and violation_codes. Representative per-episode scoring traces showing these fields are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; sha256: b8ebf9546dabb93b06b15d40152e35a3e96a9d1c98cee131bb7f8065a8b6a2b4).

Analysis, handling of missingness, and sensitivity: Primary analysis used the exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes and computed paired-bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729). The preregistered missingness policy used a complete-pair rule (exclude pairs with technical failures). A sensitivity analysis policy treating failed guarded episodes conservatively as errors was preregistered; no technical failures occurred (failed_episode_count = 0) and hence the sensitivity branch was not required. All analysis code and artifacts are archived and reconciled.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: Execution completed the full preregistered 400 episodes without any failed episodes (started_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:15:20.528566+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:37:01.389670+00:00). Provider accounting: model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task), cache_hit_count = 0, cross-condition cache reuse = false. Representative reproducibility pointers: execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b), execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).

Primary outcomes and contingency: Aggregated scoring artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv; sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) show baseline validator-clean = 200/200 and guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) is n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error). Point estimate for paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) yields 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. These numeric outputs are deterministic given the archived artifacts and appear in analysis/results.json (input_results_sha256: 9ec4eb2c...).

Repair activity and secondary estimand: Because there were zero validator-detected errors in the shared initial candidates, the bounded repair policy was never invoked (repair_count = 0). Representative guarded traces confirm repair_applied = false and repair_prompt_sha256 = null (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; sha256: 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30). Consequently, the preregistered secondary estimand—repair_success_rate (fraction of initial-error tasks corrected by repair)—is not empirically computable from these data.

Diagnostics, contamination, and reconciliation: Automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Missingness summary shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero missing or failed episodes across conditions (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; sha256: 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c). Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and that all deterministic checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; sha256: 0314c29dbc58c1315066fb146c472856066af12a615bd450d8d5f1015c360b07). These artifacts indicate the degenerate null is not attributable to execution loss or manifest mismatches.

Representative example: task-000001: the shared initial candidate (and both arm outputs) was "interface edge1 admin down\ninterface edge1 vlan 30\ninterface edge1 mtu 1600\ninterface edge1 admin up". The per-episode validator_trace records required_command_count = 4, parsed_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, validation_after.violation_count = 0, and valid = true (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; sha256: b8ebf9...). This concrete trace illustrates how the detector encodes workflow invariants (shutdown_configure_restore) and records both before/after state for auditing.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation of the degenerate null: Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract and the supplied synthetic 200-task bank, the declared generator produced validator-clean shared candidates for every task; validation_after.violation_count = 0 across episodes. This explains the degenerate null: with no initial failures there was nothing for a bounded repair loop to correct. The experiment therefore provides evidence for the conditional statement: "given a generator that produces validator-clean shared candidates under this synthetic task bank, a bounded validator/repair wrapper yields no measurable paired improvement." It does not address whether a repair loop would help when independent generation produces unsafe candidates or when validator semantics differ.

Design trade-offs and operational implications: Shared_initial_generation improves causal attribution (any discordance must come from repair) but reduces the probability of observing baseline failures. Practitioners and researchers should treat shared versus independent generation as answering different operational questions: shared_initial_generation isolates repair effectiveness conditional on specific candidate-correction capability; independent generation evaluates end-to-end production risk reduction with generator stochasticity. The archived bundle supports direct, reproducible follow-ups: (A) switch to independent condition generation (two independent model calls per task) to increase baseline failure probability and permit repair opportunities; (B) increase repair budget or enable iterative tool-assisted repair; (C) enrich the validator harm-oracle with vendor-specific semantics.

Threats to validity and practical limits: Construct validity depends on whether the deterministic verifier adequately models production harm. Our sandbox encodes workflow constraints and common failure modes (reachability, ACL/policy, routing, interface-workflow invariants), but does not capture every vendor quirk or runtime telemetry. External validity is limited by a single declared generator family (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); results do not generalize across models, larger repair budgets, adversarial prompts, or production device heterogeneity. Finally, shared_initial_generation reduced opportunities for repair; absence of observed benefit under this contract does not imply absence of benefit under independent-generation designs or targeted adversarial attacks.

Operational recommendation: To measure repair-mediated benefit in practice, deploy a staggered evaluation matrix that crosses: (1) shared vs independent generation, (2) repair budget depth, and (3) validator fidelity. The archived manifests, per-episode traces, and reconciliation artifacts provide a reproducible starting point for such factorial follow-ups.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline under a shared_initial_generation contract. For the synthetic 200-task bank and declared generator (gpt-5-mini) used here, every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: both baseline and guarded arms were validator-clean on all tasks, giving an exact paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked, so repair efficacy was unobserved. These artifact-grounded results show that preregistered contract choices (shared vs independent generation), task-bank challenge level, validator fidelity, and repair policy jointly determine whether verifier assistance yields an observable benefit. The archived execution bundle contains task manifest, raw responses, per-episode validator traces, paired contingency tables, and reconciliation logs needed to reproduce the run and to design follow-ups that trade off generator variance and repair opportunity to quantify repair-mediated gains in realistic settings.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-style sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single declared model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

The preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduced the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
